Measured on twelve fixtures - widget-t-literal (/T (the field) -> "the field"), widget-t-empty (/T () -> the empty string), widget-t-name (/T as a NAME -> not read), widget-t-merged (the /Parent is a field carrying /T (parent field) -> "parent field"), widget-t-mergedname (both -> "parent field.child too") and the nine widget-t-extra fixtures, one per other key including a /DA written as a text string.  The harness compares this over the fixtures that name their widgets, with seven red controls over the spellings
entries.reason: and the answer for a widget that NAMES NOTHING is not implementable, which is why the row is inert rather than implemented.  The host SYNTHESISES a name whose number is a PROCESS-GLOBAL counter: five fixtures opened in order in one process answer text0..text2, then text3..text4, then text5..text6, then text7, then text8..text9 - so it does not restart per document and is not a property of any file.  An earlier version of this reason said the name was synthesised BY DOCUMENT POSITION and that a widget carrying /T answered the synthesised name anyway; both halves were wrong. widget-mixed.pdf is the fixture that shows the first: its two widgets are the third and fifth of five annotations and answered text7 and text8, because four files had been opened before them.  The second was a FIXTURE defect - /DA is a TEXT STRING, /DA (/Helv 12 Tf 0 g), and that fixture wrote the content-stream operators bare into the dictionary, which is a syntax error: CG_PDF_VERBOSE reports "encountered unexpected symbol `Tf'" and the host then answers NO ANNOTATIONS for the page, so the widget carrying /T was not in -annotations at all.  Written as the format makes it the same widget answers "the field", and widget-values.pdf keeps all three of its annotations

entries.effect: 1 when /AS or /V names the widget's ON-STATE, or when BOTH name a state that is not /Off; and -1 for a widget that is not a BUTTON.  Three clauses over 31 measured shapes, and the on-state is -buttonWidgetStateString's answer.  Each clause has a fixture that says so: /AS /Yes with no /V is 1 (button-as-alone) and /V /Yes with no /AS is ALSO 1 (button-v-only), so neither key can be the only one; the BOTH clause covers /AS /On with /V /On (button-as-and-v) and /AS /On with /V /Yes (button-asoff-von), which is where the coordinator's hypothesis - /V names the SAME state /AS names - is REFUTED, because /AS names /On and /V names /Yes and the answer is still 1; and a /V of /Off does not count, which button-asoff-von's /AS /On with /V /Off (0) fixes.  -1: every /Tx answers -1 whatever it carries (text-as, four states), and so do all six button-merged-* shapes, whose /Btn FIELD carries the /FT while the widget reaches it through /Parent - so the field type is NOT inherited
